content.text:
I changed SCIM user deletion so it fires `UserRemovedEvent`, the same as Admin REST does. I haven't compiled it or run any tests.

In `UserResourceTypeProvider.onDelete` (in `scim/model`), the code called `session.users().removeUser(realm, model)`. That removes the user from the store but never publishes the event. It now calls `new UserManager(session).removeUser(realm, model)`, which is what `UserResource` uses for Admin REST deletes. `UserManager` publishes the event after a successful removal. Session cleanup, login-failure counters, authorization-store sync and workflow state listen for that event, so they now run for SCIM deletes too. I also added the `UserManager` import.

I did not use the graph for this task. The repo had no index, and a plain grep found the call site directly.
